title: Evaluating QAOA expectation values can be as hard as counting optimal solutions
summary: Evaluating expectation values is a critical task for variational quantum eigensolvers, parameterized quantum circuits, and many other quantum algorithms. We consider the well-studied case of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for the MaxCut problem. Recent work of Wang et al. [arXiv:2511.20212] showed this task to be NP-hard in general for any QAOA depth $p\geq 2$, complementing past results showing efficiently computable formulas for $p=1$ with arbitrary problem graphs.
